title: Learning to sail the hard way
text: Nobody had warned me {{1}} handling a dinghy was so physical. Within minutes of leaving the shore, my arms were aching and I was completely soaked. My instructor shouted instructions, {{2}} of which I could understand over the wind. Worst of {{3}} , the boat tipped and I ended up in the water. Despite {{4}} thoroughly humiliating, the experience taught me more in an hour than weeks of theory. I learned to respect the weather, to read the water and, {{5}} importantly, to laugh at myself. By the end of the week I could sail a triangular course {{6}} capsizing once. Now, whenever I struggle {{7}} something new, I remind {{8}} how much can be learned by falling in.
